questions.q: Name the two iodinated hormones secreted by the thyroid follicular cells and state the essential dietary element required for their synthesis.
questions.a: The thyroid follicular cells secrete thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3); iodine is the essential dietary element required for their synthesis. A wrong answer (e.g., naming calcitonin as an iodinated hormone or stating iron is needed) reveals confusion between thyroid hormone types and the specific role of iodine in thyronine structure.

questions.q: Explain why a person living in the Himalayan foothills with no access to iodized salt develops a goitre, linking the dietary deficiency to the hormonal feedback loop.
questions.a: Iodine deficiency reduces T3/T4 synthesis → low blood T3/T4 removes negative inhibition on hypothalamus and anterior pituitary → increased TRH and TSH secretion → sustained TSH stimulation causes thyroid follicular hypertrophy and hyperplasia → visible goitre. A wrong answer that omits the feedback loop (e.g., "thyroid enlarges to trap more iodine" without mentioning TSH) shows lack of understanding of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis.

questions.q: A patient has a blood calcium level of 8.5 mg/dL (normal 9-11 mg/dL). Predict which hormone's secretion will increase and describe its three target organs and actions to restore calcium homeostasis.
questions.a: Low blood Ca²⁺ stimulates parathyroid chief cells to secrete PTH. PTH acts on: (1) bones – stimulates osteoclasts to resorb bone matrix releasing Ca²⁺; (2) kidneys – enhances Ca²⁺ reabsorption in distal tubules and increases 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D₃ synthesis; (3) intestine – via vitamin D, increases Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food. A wrong answer that names calcitonin or omits the renal vitamin D step reveals misunderstanding of the hypercalcemic hormone and its indirect intestinal action.

questions.q: Compare and contrast the roles of calcitonin and PTH in calcium homeostasis, including their cellular sources, stimuli for secretion, and overall effect on blood calcium.
questions.a: Calcitonin is secreted by thyroid parafollicular (C) cells in response to high blood Ca²⁺; it inhibits osteoclast activity and increases renal Ca²⁺ excretion, lowering blood Ca²⁺. PTH is secreted by parathyroid chief cells in response to low blood Ca²⁺; it stimulates osteoclasts, renal reabsorption, and vitamin D synthesis, raising blood Ca²⁺. They are antagonistic. A wrong answer that swaps the stimuli or states both increase blood calcium shows confusion about the direction of each hormone's action and the concept of antagonistic regulation.

questions.q: Evaluate the statement: "Cretinism and myxoedema are both caused by hypothyroidism, so they have identical symptoms and age of onset." Justify your evaluation.
questions.a: The statement is false. Cretinism results from hypothyroidism during fetal/neonatal development (maternal iodine deficiency or congenital defect) causing irreversible stunted growth, mental retardation, deaf-mutism, and abnormal skin. Myxoedema occurs in adults, causing puffy skin, low metabolic rate, weight gain, cold intolerance, and menstrual irregularities. The difference lies in the critical developmental window: thyroid hormones are essential for CNS maturation and skeletal growth in early life. A wrong answer that treats them as identical ignores the developmental role of thyroid hormones.

questions.q: Design a simple dietary intervention study to test whether iodized salt prevents goitre in a village population, specifying the control group, duration, and measurable outcome.
questions.a: Randomly assign households to receive either iodized salt (intervention) or non-iodized salt (control) for 12 months. Measure thyroid volume by ultrasound and urinary iodine concentration at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Outcome: reduction in goitre prevalence and increased urinary iodine in intervention group. A poor design (e.g., no control group, short duration, only self-reported neck swelling) reveals inability to apply experimental design principles to a public health nutrition problem.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The thyroid gland is a bilobed endocrine gland located anterior to the trachea that synthesizes iodinated hormones thyroxine (T4) and ______ (T3) regulating basal metabolic rate of lipids, carbohydrates, and proteins, and also secretes calcitonin (thyrocalcitonin) which lowers blood calcium levels.

Fill in the blank: Observe a person in your neighborhood with a visible swelling at the base of the neck – this is a goitre, often caused by iodine ______ in the diet, common in inland areas of India where soil lacks iodine.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Student can explain the negative feedback loop between hypothalamus-pituitary-thyroid axis, describe the antagonistic roles of calcitonin and PTH in calcium homeostasis with specific target organs, and predict the physiological consequences of hypo/hypersecretion of each hormone (goitre, cretinism, Graves' disease, tetany, osteoporosis).
